newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish bonds mark time ahead of US data, Amsterdam.
newsitem.headline: Danish bonds mark time ahead of US data, Amsterdam.

text.p: Danish bond prices were near static on Friday, in a reasonably optimistic market looking ahead to the afternoon's U.S. May PPI data and the EU's Amsterdam summit early next week.
"The market is a little cautious, but the undertone is fine. We fell a little back this morning on profit-taking, an EMU deal would be good news for U.S. bonds," one dealer said.

The benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 was 0.03 point down on Thursday's close at 111.95, while the forthcoming seven percent 2007 benchmark, which takes over on September 1, was up 0.04 point at 104.59, both down from earlier highs.
Turnover was 1.7 billion crowns for the 2006 benchmark and 400 million for the 2007 benchmark-to-be.
The 2006's June future rose 0.49 point to 111.99 with 418 contracts traded. The six percent mortgage bond due 2026 gained 0.30 point to 90.30.
The crown traded at 3.8069 per mark at 1130 GMT, down slightly from around 3.8065 at the opening.
The 2006's 10-year yield gap with Germany was one basis point wider at 46 basis points, while the 2007-bund differential was unchanged at 65 bps.
